story.title: Karoline Leavitt to Depart as White House Press Secretary
story.summary: Karoline Leavitt will step down from her role as White House press secretary at the end of the month, as announced by President Donald Trump. Leavitt described her decision as bittersweet, having recently returned to work after the birth of her second child. She is noted for being the youngest person to hold the position and will continue as a senior advisor following her departure.

explore_lenses.label: What changes at the end of August?
explore_lenses.title: Leavitt leaves the White House staff role
explore_lenses.summary: Leavitt is set to stop serving as press secretary at the end of August, ending a White House appointment she held from January 2025. Trump has said she will remain in his political orbit as an outside adviser, but the public announcement does not define that role's duties or employment terms.

claims.text: Leavitt will leave the press secretary position at the end of August, according to Trump's announcement and Leavitt's subsequent statement.
Her public financial disclosure identifies her as a non-career White House press secretary appointed on January 20, 2025.

Trump said Leavitt would become one of his “top outside advisors” and an influential Republican voice ahead of the midterm elections; that is Trump's stated plan, not a publicly detailed job description.

explore_lenses.label: Who will run press briefings next?
explore_lenses.title: No successor has been announced
explore_lenses.summary: The administration has not identified a replacement or interim press secretary. Its existing communications roster includes a principal deputy press secretary, but there is no public confirmation that person will take the top role.

claims.text: Trump did not identify a replacement for Leavitt in his announcement.
The White House's January 2025 communications appointments named Harrison Fields as principal deputy press secretary, alongside deputy press secretaries Anna Kelly and Kush Desai.
During Leavitt's maternity leave, Vice President JD Vance, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent were among officials who held briefing-room press conferences.

explore_lenses.label: How do Leavitt and Trump explain it?
explore_lenses.title: They frame it as a family-driven departure
explore_lenses.summary: Leavitt says the demands of the job conflicted with the time she wanted to give her two young children after returning from maternity leave. Trump publicly praised her work and linked her planned outside-adviser role to Republican midterm efforts.

claims.text: Leavitt described her decision as “bittersweet” and said she concluded she could not give both the press secretary job and her two children the time and attention they deserved.
She returned to the White House podium after the May birth of her daughter, Viviana; she also has a 2-year-old son.
Trump said he understood and respected her decision and characterized Leavitt as a trusted aide who would remain influential in Republican politics.

story_report.summary: Karoline Leavitt will step down as White House press secretary at the end of August, President Donald Trump announced, leaving the administration without a publicly named successor. Leavitt, the youngest person to hold the post, said the decision followed her recent return from maternity leave. Trump has said she will become one of his top outside advisers and remain a Republican voice before the midterm elections, though the nature of that role has not been publicly detailed.

sections.heading: Leavitt Explains Her Departure
sections.body: Leavitt described her decision as “bittersweet,” saying she had concluded she could not give both the press secretary’s job and her two children the time and attention they deserved. She returned to the White House podium after the May birth of her daughter, Viviana, and also has a 2-year-old son. Trump said he understood and respected the decision, calling her a trusted aide who would remain influential in Republican politics.

sections.heading: White House Press Office Succession
sections.body: Trump did not name a replacement in his announcement. The White House’s January 2025 communications appointments listed Harrison Fields as principal deputy press secretary and Anna Kelly and Kush Desai as deputy press secretaries. During Leavitt’s maternity leave, Vice President JD Vance, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent were among officials who held briefing-room press conferences.

unresolved.text: It remains unclear whether the White House will promote a current press-office official, use an interim spokesperson or choose someone from outside the existing team.
No public announcement specifies whether Leavitt’s outside-adviser role will be formal, paid or tied to a particular organization.

related_stories.title: Putin Observes Naval Drills Before Controversial Visit to Disputed Kuril Islands
related_stories.summary: President Vladimir Putin observed naval exercises off Sakhalin Island before making a controversial visit to the Kuril Islands, which Japan claims. This visit has prompted strong protests from Japan, with officials labeling it 'unacceptable' and summoning the Russian ambassador to express their discontent. This marks the first visit by a Russian leader to the disputed islands since they were seized by the Soviet Union in 1945.
